messages.subject: Priors for Occupancy
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I am still very new to the Bayesian approach. I am fortunate in that I have access to both historical and contemporary occupancy data for a rare freshwater fish. With that in mind, the Bayesian approach seemed to be best suited for tackling the research objectives of the project that I'm currently working on. With that in mind, I have a couple of questions:

1.  What distributions seem to work best for specifying informative priors on psi and p and betas for covariates? In this case, I'd be using estimates of psi, p, and the betas from the historical models as priors for the contemporary models.

2.  There appears to be remarkably mixed views on DIC vs. WAIC in the literature. Recent papers (Stevens & Conway, 2019) suggest that neither method is appropriate; rather they suggest using logarithmic scoring rule).  However, it seems that this assumption is mostly based on the premise that the analyst would use out-of-sample data to test the model's predictive performance. I think I read somewhere that other users on this forum more or less reached this same assertion. What are your opinions?

Any guidance, as always, is much appreciated.

Thanks!

-Josh

messages.subject: RE: Priors for Occupancy
messages.body_plain:
Dear Josh,

about 1. it is best to simply analyse all data in one single model in what could be called an integrated model. In that way, the "flux" of the information from the old to the new data happens automatically. When you fit one model to the old data and then distill the information about the resulting estimates into some distribution to be used as a prior in the analysis for the new data, you simply take two steps and do things more approximately, instead of doing all at once and exact. --- And of course, in such a combined analysis you can then more directly compare distribution between then and now, full with proper uncertainty. Sure this is one objective of your analysis.

about 2: don't know.

Best regards  --- Marc

Hi everyone,

Please help us spread the word. Thanks.

A one-year postdoc (with possible extension) is available in the Chandler Lab <https://nam04.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fchandlerlab.uga.edu%2F&data=04%...%40tamuk.edu%7C86562d3da6bd43c6629508d88cd419a0%7C17420fd64d7546859adf7a650964dbcf%7C0%7C1%7C637414190296145431%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C3000&sdata=plac%2B096ns3k%2FCZ2cjAWQhVtu1WlC9g1jhgl0jEUycA%3D&reserved=0> at the University of Georgia. The focus of the position will be on understanding interactions between animal movement, resource selection, and survival. Available datasets include >500,000 GPS telemetry locations and mortality information on 250 white-tailed deer, and 3 years of data from 180 cameras in the core of the Florida panther range. A secondary emphasis will be on software development to support US Fish and Wildlife Service monitoring efforts. Applicants experienced with movement models, survival models, and spatial capture-recapture models are encouraged to apply. Applicants should have experience with R and Bayesian inference. The postdoc will be jointly supervised by Richard Chandler and Mike Cherry (Caesar Kleberg Wildlife Research Institute). The anticipated start date is between January 15 and March 1, 2021. Preference will be given to applicants interested in moving to Athens, GA, but relocation is not required. Apply here <https://nam04.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.ugajobsearch.com%2Fpostings%2F177085&data=04%...%40tamuk.edu%7C86562d3da6bd43c6629508d88cd419a0%7C17420fd64d7546859adf7a650964dbcf%7C0%7C1%7C637414190296155433%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C3000&sdata=B2MUN0SfeAIop5VcykyLalVFzW%2FkZMPv7qoog2ZCbmM%3D&reserved=0>, and send a single PDF with letter of interest, CV, and contact information for three references to rcha...@warnell.uga.edu by December 18, 2020.

Richard

Marc,

Thank you for the quick reply.

Using your suggestion I went back and examined the code, but, I cannot seem to identify the error. If you or anyone else would be willing to give

data<-read.csv("data.csv", header = T, row.names = "ID")

#detection data
y<-data[,2:3]
n<-nrow(data)
n.occas<- ncol(y)

#Site Covariates
Period<- as.integer(data$Period)
DA<- log(data[,17])
PC1<- data[,13]
PC2<- data[,14]
Area<- log(data[,15])
Bar.Type<- log(data[,16])
Sinuosity<- log(data[,18])

#observation covariates
Effort<- data[,6:7]

#Single-Season Occupancy Model with Observation Covariate and Random Intercept on Psi (Period)
#Organize Data into List for input into JAGS
jags.data<-list(y=y,n.sites=n,n.occas=n.occas, Effort=Effort, Period=Period, nCat=2)

########################
require(jagsUI)
sink("model.jags.txt")
cat("
model{

# Priors
  for(i in 1:nCat) {
    psi[i] ~ dunif(0,1)
    }
alpha.p ~ dnorm(0, 0.01)
beta1.p ~ dnorm(0, 0.01)

# Likelihood
# Ecological model for the partially observed true state
for (i in 1:n.sites) {
   z[i] ~ dbern(psi[Period[i]])                # True occurrence z at site i

   # Observation model for the observations
    for (j in 1:n.occas) {
      y[i,j] ~ dbern(mu.p[i,j]) # Detection-nondetection at i and j
      mu.p[i,j] <- z[i] * p[i,j]
      logit(p[i,j]) <- alpha.p + beta1.p * Effort[i,j]
      } #j
   } #i
   site.occup<- sum(z[])
    }
    ", fill=TRUE)
sink()

messages.body_plain:
I'm working with a dataset where approximately 39% of the "sites" are associated with only 2 detections. Obviously it would be nice if only a few sites had only 2 or more surveys, but this is the data I am working with. I'm running a basic single-season model with covariates on occupancy and detection using jagSUI.

My questions are:

Should I drop the remaining surveys for sites with >2 if the model does not run smoothly?

Also: I've tried running the model with all of the data, but I'm confronted with the following error "one node produced an error, Error in node y[1,1]. Node inconsistent with parents". I read on the forum that in order for these models to work, the user should first supply JAGs with a value for Z (which I did) when establishing initial values. However, I'm still getting an error. Any thoughts on this?

Here is the code; data is attached below.  Thanks.

#####Bayesian Hierarchical Models using JAGS (Single-Season Occupany Models)
##MUST DOWNLOAD JAGS for this to work!
#Model Set for All Rivers
data<-read.csv("pd_occu.csv", header = T, row.names = "ID")

#detection data; rows are sites columns are detection replicates
y<-data[,2:5]
n<-nrow(data)
n.occas<- ncol(y)

#Site Covariates
Period<- as.integer(data$Period)+1
DA<- log(data[,17])
PC1<- data[,13]
PC2<- data[,14]
Area<- log(data[,15])
Bar.Type<- log(data[,16])
Sinuosity<- log(data[,18])

##Drop Drainage Area & PC2, highly correlated
Covariates<- as.matrix(cbind(PC1, Area, Bar.Type, Sinuosity))

cor(Covariates)

#observation covariates
Effort<- data[,6:9]

#data for no-covariate model
jags.data<-list(y=y,n.sites=n,n.occas=n.occas)

##Simple Single-Season Occupancy Model, Constant Detection
########################
require(jagsUI)
sink("occupancy.txt")
cat("
    model{
    #priors
    psi~dbeta(1,1)
    p~dbeta(1,1)
    for(i in 1:n.sites)
    {
    z[i]~dbern(psi)
    p.eff[i]<-z[i]*p
    for (j in 1:n.occas)
    {
    y[i,j]~dbern(p.eff[i])
    }

    }
    site.occup<-sum(z[])
    }
    ",fill=TRUE)
sink()

##vector to set initial occupancy state to 1 if 1 or more detection occurred at site.  speeds up BUGS, essential for JAGS
#JAGS can tempermental with initial values for params and NAs
z.init<-apply(jags.data$y,1,max)
initial<-function()list(p=runif(1,0,1),psi=runif(1,0,1),z=z.init)
params<-c("psi","p","site.occup")
inits<-list(initial(),initial(),initial())
occu_null <- jagsUI(data=jags.data, inits, parameters.to.save=params, model.file="occupancy.txt",n.thin = 5,n.chains = 3, n.burnin = 5000, n.iter =10000,parallel=TRUE)

Thanks,

Josh

messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,
I'm trying to calculate the "log scoring rule" from the Stevens & Conway (2019) <https://esajournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/ecs2.2748> paper* using their code and simulated occupancy data (325 sites, 4 years, 6 visits per site per year). I split the data into 4 parts (260 sites) for training and 1 part (65 sites) for testing. The idea is to ultimately do this five times for a 5-fold cross validation version of this metric. The code runs fine if I comment out the log-scoring calculation part. But when it is included I get this error:
"Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) :
  3 nodes produced errors; first error: RUNTIME ERROR:
Failed check for discrete-valued parameters in function :"

The code to simulate the data in R and run the model in JAGS are below (only takes a minute or two to run).  Can anyone help me figure out what is causing this error?

Thanks very much,

Mike

*Stevens, B. S., & Conway, C. J. (2019). Predicting species distributions: unifying model selection and scale optimization for multi‐scale occupancy models. Ecosphere, 10(5), e02748.

#####################################
###### SIMULATE 4 YEARS OF 6-VISIT DETECTION / NON-DETECTION AT 325 SITES
###### WITH ONE COVARIATE FOR PSI AND ONE FOR P
#####################################

# (data simulation code adapted from Kery & Royle AHM1)

# Choose sample sizes and prepare obs. data array y
n.sites <- 325                      # Number of sites
J <-  6                        # Number of presence/absence measurements per site per year
y1 <-
  matrix(NA, nrow = n.sites, ncol = J) # to contain the obs. data, year 1
y2 <-
  matrix(NA, nrow = n.sites, ncol = J) # to contain the obs. data, year 2
y3 <-
  matrix(NA, nrow = n.sites, ncol = J) # to contain the obs. data, year 3
y4 <-
  matrix(NA, nrow = n.sites, ncol = J) # to contain the obs. data, year 4

# Create a covariate called vegHt
set.seed(110)
vegHt <- runif(n.sites,-1, 1)

# Choose parameter values for occupancy model and compute occupancy
beta0 <- -2                    # Logit-scale intercept
beta1 <- 2                    # Logit-scale slope for vegHt
psi <- plogis(beta0 + beta1 * vegHt) # Occupancy probability
# plot(vegHt, psi, ylim = c(0,1), lwd = 3) # Plot psi relationship

# Now visit each site and observe presence/absence perfectly
set.seed(120)
z1 <- rbinom(n.sites, 1, psi)        # True presence/absence year 1
set.seed(130)
z2 <- rbinom(n.sites, 1, psi)        # True presence/absence year 2
set.seed(140)
z3 <- rbinom(n.sites, 1, psi)        # True presence/absence year 3
set.seed(150)
z4 <- rbinom(n.sites, 1, psi)        # True presence/absence year 4

# Create a covariate called wind
set.seed(160)
wind1 <- array(runif(n.sites * J,-1, 1), dim = c(n.sites, J))
set.seed(170)
wind2 <- array(runif(n.sites * J,-1, 1), dim = c(n.sites, J))
set.seed(180)
wind3 <- array(runif(n.sites * J,-1, 1), dim = c(n.sites, J))
set.seed(190)
wind4 <- array(runif(n.sites * J,-1, 1), dim = c(n.sites, J))

# Choose parameter values for measurement error model and compute detectability
alpha0 <- -1                        # Logit-scale intercept
alpha1 <- -3                        # Logit-scale slope for wind
p1 <- plogis(alpha0 + alpha1 * wind1) # Detection probability
p2 <- plogis(alpha0 + alpha1 * wind2) # Detection probability
p3 <- plogis(alpha0 + alpha1 * wind3) # Detection probability
p4 <- plogis(alpha0 + alpha1 * wind4) # Detection probability

#plot(p1 ~ wind1, ylim = c(0,1))     # Look at relationship

# Take J = 6 presence/absence measurements at each site in each year
set.seed(200)
for (j in 1:J) {
  y1[, j] <- rbinom(n.sites, z1, p1[, j])
}

set.seed(210)
for (j in 1:J) {
  y2[, j] <- rbinom(n.sites, z2, p2[, j])
}

set.seed(220)
for (j in 1:J) {
  y3[, j] <- rbinom(n.sites, z3, p3[, j])
}

set.seed(230)
for (j in 1:J) {
  y4[, j] <- rbinom(n.sites, z4, p4[, j])
}

#####################################
###### FORMAT DATA FOR THE STEVENS & CONWAY, ECOSPHERE (2019) MODEL
###### RUN THE MODEL IN JAGS
#####################################

T = 4 # number of years sampled
n = c(n.sites, n.sites, n.sites, n.sites)
y = cbind(c(t(y1)), c(t(y2)), c(t(y3)), c(t(y4)))
sites.list = list()
for (s in 1:n.sites) {
  sites.list[[s]] = rep(s, J)
}
sites <- matrix(rep(do.call("c", sites.list), T), ncol = T)
# the site-level covariate
vegHt <- vegHt
# obs-level covariate
wind = cbind(c(t(wind1)), c(t(wind2)), c(t(wind3)), c(t(wind4)))

# Now separating out into "training" and "testing" data set
frac <-
  4 / 5 # fraction to use for training data set (must split data set evenly)
n.sites.train <- n.sites * frac
n.sites.test <- n.sites * (1 - frac)
T <- T
T2 <- T
n.train <- n * frac
n.test <- n * (1 - frac)
y.train <- y[1:(nrow(y) * frac), ]
y.test <- y[((nrow(y) * frac) + 1):nrow(y), ]
sites.train <- sites[1:(nrow(sites) * frac), ]
sites.test <- sites[((nrow(sites) * frac) + 1):nrow(sites), ]
vegHt.train <- vegHt[1:(length(vegHt) * frac)]
vegHt.test <- vegHt[((length(vegHt) * frac) + 1):length(vegHt)]
wind.train <- wind[1:(nrow(y) * frac), ]
wind.test <- wind[((nrow(y) * frac) + 1):nrow(y), ]
total.visits <- matrix(rep(J, n.sites * frac * T), ncol = T)

jags_data = list(
  n.sites = n.sites.train,
  T = T,
  n = n.train,
  y = y.train,
  sites = sites.train,
  vegHt = vegHt.train,
  wind = wind.train,
  T2 = T,
  sites2 = n.test,
  total.visits = total.visits,
  vegHt2 = vegHt.test,
  wind2 = wind.test,
  y2 = y.test
)

# save the model file
sink("SC_mod.txt")

cat(
  "
  model {

    ####################
    #Priors
    ####################

    #detection parameters
    alpha[1] ~ dt(0, 1/6.25, 1)    #cauchy(0, 2.5) priors
    alpha[2] ~ dt(0, 1/6.25, 1)

    #occupancy covariates
    beta[1] ~ dt(0, 1/6.25, 1)
    beta[2] ~ dt(0, 1/6.25, 1)

    ####################
    #Likelihood
    ####################

    #likelihood for latent states

    for(s in 1:n.sites){                        #n.sites = no. of field sampling locations
      for(t in 1:T){                        #T = no. of years sampled
        z[s,t] ~ dbern(psi[s,t])            #z[s,t] = latent occupancy state at site s in year t

        #site-specific occupancy probability
        l.psi[s,t] <- beta[1] + beta[2]*vegHt[s]
        psi[s,t] <- exp(l.psi[s,t])/(1+exp(l.psi[s,t]))
      }
    }

    #likelihood for observations in vertical format (not all sites sampled every year: i = ith observation in year t)

    for(t in 1:T){
      for(i in 1:n[t]){                    #n = vector of number of sites sampled by year

        #sampling-event specific detection probability
        l.p[i,t] <- alpha[1] + alpha[2]*wind[i,t]
        p[i,t] <- exp(l.p[i,t])/(1+exp(l.p[i,t]))
        eff.p[i,t] <- z[sites[i,t],t]*p[i,t]        #sites = matrix of site numbers (s indices from above) for observation i in year t
        y[i,t] ~ dbern(eff.p[i,t])
      }
    }

    #Calculating integrated likelihood and log-posterior predictive scores for testing data set

     for(t in 1:T2){                            # T = no. of years sampled in testing data set
         for(s in 1:sites2[t]){                    # sites2 = vector of no. of sites in testing data by year
                 l.psi2[s,t] <- beta[1] + beta[2]*vegHt2[s]
                 psi2[s,t] <- exp(l.psi2[s,t])/(1+exp(l.psi2[s,t]))
             for(v in 1:total.visits[s,t]){

                 #total.visits = matrix with total number of visits for site s in year t in testing data
                 #calculate p for each visit as a function of covariate values and regression coefficients

                 l.pnew[s,v,t] <- alpha[1] + alpha[2]*wind2[s,v,t]
                 p.new <http://p.new>[s,v,t] <- exp(l.pnew[s,v,t])/(1+exp(l.pnew[s,v,t]))
                 prob1[s,v,t] <- pow(p.new <http://p.new>[s,v,t], y2[s,v,t])*pow((1-p.new <http://1-p.new>[s,v,t]),(1-y2[s,v,t]))
                 prob2[s,v,t] <- 1-p.new <http://1-p.new>[s,v,t]
             }

             #see Appendix S1 for integrated likelihood and log-score formulae
             term1[s,t] <- indicator[s,t]*psi2[s,t]*prod(prob1[s,1:total.visits[s,t],t])
             term2[s,t] <- (1-indicator[s,t])*((1-psi2[s,t]) + psi2[s,t]*prod(prob2[s,1:total.visits[s,t],t]))
             y.prob[s,t] <- term1[s,t] + term2[s,t]
             lprob.y[s,t] <- log(y.prob[s,t])
         }
         score.t[t] <- sum(lprob.y[1:sites2[t],t])        #see S1.2
     }
     l.score <- -2*sum(score.t)

  }
"
)

sink()

# Inits
z.wide <- as.matrix(aggregate(y, by = list(sites[, 1]), max)[2:5])
z.wide.train <- z.wide[1:(nrow(z.wide) * frac), ]
inits <- function() {
  list(
    z = z.wide.train,
    alpha = c(-1,-3) + rnorm(2),
    beta = c(-2, 2) + rnorm(2)
  )
}

# Parameters monitored
params <- c("alpha", "beta", "l.score")

# MCMC settings
ni <- 20000
nt <- 10
nb <- 10000
nc <- 3

# Call JAGS from R and summarize posteriors
SCtest <-
  jagsUI::jags(
    jags_data,
    inits = inits,
    params,
    "SC_mod.txt",
    n.chains = nc,
    n.thin = nt,
    n.iter = ni,
    n.burnin = nb,
    parallel = TRUE
  )

Because of the way the supplied data 'sites2' is being calculated, JAGS is interpreting it as a float instead of an integer (though it looks like an integer in R), and thus not allowing it to be used as an index. You can fix this by wrapping sites2 in as.integer() when creating the input data:

jags_data = list(
  n.sites = n.sites.train,
  T = T,
  n = n.train,
  y = y.train,
  sites = sites.train,
  vegHt = vegHt.train,
  wind = wind.train,
  T2 = T,

  sites2 = as.integer(n.test), #change here

  total.visits = total.visits,
  vegHt2 = vegHt.test,
  wind2 = wind.test,
  y2 = y.test
)

With this fix your model got past this particular error but ran into another because data 'indicator' is missing.

Ken

#####################################
###### SIMULATE 4 YEARS OF 6-VISIT DETECTION / NON-DETECTION AT 325 SITES
###### WITH ONE COVARIATE FOR PSI AND ONE FOR P
#####################################

# (data simulation code adapted from Kery & Royle AHM1)

# Choose sample sizes and prepare obs. data array y
n.sites <- 325                      # Number of sites
J <-  6                        # Number of presence/absence measurements per site per year
y1 <-
  matrix(NA, nrow = n.sites, ncol = J) # to contain the obs. data, year 1
y2 <-
  matrix(NA, nrow = n.sites, ncol = J) # to contain the obs. data, year 2
y3 <-
  matrix(NA, nrow = n.sites, ncol = J) # to contain the obs. data, year 3
y4 <-
  matrix(NA, nrow = n.sites, ncol = J) # to contain the obs. data, year 4

# Create a covariate called vegHt
set.seed(110)
vegHt <- runif(n.sites,-1, 1)

# Choose parameter values for occupancy model and compute occupancy
beta0 <- -2                    # Logit-scale intercept
beta1 <- 2                    # Logit-scale slope for vegHt
psi <- plogis(beta0 + beta1 * vegHt) # Occupancy probability
# plot(vegHt, psi, ylim = c(0,1), lwd = 3) # Plot psi relationship

# Now visit each site and observe presence/absence perfectly
set.seed(120)
z1 <- rbinom(n.sites, 1, psi)        # True presence/absence year 1
set.seed(130)
z2 <- rbinom(n.sites, 1, psi)        # True presence/absence year 2
set.seed(140)
z3 <- rbinom(n.sites, 1, psi)        # True presence/absence year 3
set.seed(150)
z4 <- rbinom(n.sites, 1, psi)        # True presence/absence year 4

# Create a covariate called wind
set.seed(160)
wind1 <- array(runif(n.sites * J,-1, 1), dim = c(n.sites, J))
set.seed(170)
wind2 <- array(runif(n.sites * J,-1, 1), dim = c(n.sites, J))
set.seed(180)
wind3 <- array(runif(n.sites * J,-1, 1), dim = c(n.sites, J))
set.seed(190)
wind4 <- array(runif(n.sites * J,-1, 1), dim = c(n.sites, J))

# Choose parameter values for measurement error model and compute detectability
alpha0 <- -1                        # Logit-scale intercept
alpha1 <- -3                        # Logit-scale slope for wind
p1 <- plogis(alpha0 + alpha1 * wind1) # Detection probability
p2 <- plogis(alpha0 + alpha1 * wind2) # Detection probability
p3 <- plogis(alpha0 + alpha1 * wind3) # Detection probability
p4 <- plogis(alpha0 + alpha1 * wind4) # Detection probability

#plot(p1 ~ wind1, ylim = c(0,1))     # Look at relationship

# Take J = 6 presence/absence measurements at each site in each year
set.seed(200)
for (j in 1:J) {
  y1[, j] <- rbinom(n.sites, z1, p1[, j])
}

set.seed(210)
for (j in 1:J) {
  y2[, j] <- rbinom(n.sites, z2, p2[, j])
}

set.seed(220)
for (j in 1:J) {
  y3[, j] <- rbinom(n.sites, z3, p3[, j])
}

set.seed(230)
for (j in 1:J) {
  y4[, j] <- rbinom(n.sites, z4, p4[, j])
}

#####################################
###### FORMAT DATA FOR THE STEVENS & CONWAY, ECOSPHERE (2019) MODEL
###### RUN THE MODEL IN JAGS
#####################################

T = 4 # number of years sampled
n = c(n.sites, n.sites, n.sites, n.sites)
y = cbind(c(t(y1)), c(t(y2)), c(t(y3)), c(t(y4)))
sites.list = list()
for (s in 1:n.sites) {
  sites.list[[s]] = rep(s, J)
}
sites <- matrix(rep(do.call("c", sites.list), T), ncol = T)
# the site-level covariate
vegHt <- vegHt
# obs-level covariate
wind = cbind(c(t(wind1)), c(t(wind2)), c(t(wind3)), c(t(wind4)))

# Now separating out into "training" and "testing" data set
frac <-
  4 / 5 # fraction to use for training data set (must split data set evenly)

n.sites.train <- as.integer(as.character(n.sites * frac))
n.sites.test <- as.integer(as.character(n.sites * (1 - frac)))

T <- T
T2 <- T

n.train <- as.integer(as.character(n * frac))
n.test <- as.integer(as.character(n * (1 - frac)))

y.train <- y[1:(nrow(y) * frac), ]
y.test <- y[((nrow(y) * frac) + 1):nrow(y), ]
sites.train <- sites[1:(nrow(sites) * frac), ]
sites.test <- sites[((nrow(sites) * frac) + 1):nrow(sites), ]
vegHt.train <- vegHt[1:(length(vegHt) * frac)]
vegHt.test <- vegHt[((length(vegHt) * frac) + 1):length(vegHt)]
wind.train <- wind[1:(nrow(y) * frac), ]
wind.test <- wind[((nrow(y) * frac) + 1):nrow(y), ]

total.visits <- matrix(rep(J, n.sites.test*T), ncol = T)

z.wide <- as.matrix(aggregate(y, by = list(sites[, 1]), max)[2:5])
z.wide.train <- z.wide[1:(nrow(z.wide) * frac), ]

z.wide.test <- z.wide[((nrow(z.wide) * frac) + 1):nrow(z.wide),]

jags_data = list(
  n.sites = n.sites.train,
  T = T,
  n = n.train,
  y = y.train,
  sites = sites.train,
  vegHt = vegHt.train,
  wind = wind.train,
  T2 = T,
  sites2 = as.integer(n.test),

  total.visits = total.visits,
  vegHt2 = vegHt.test,
  wind2 = wind.test,

  y2 = y.test,
  indicator = z.wide.test

)

# save the model file
sink("SC_mod.txt")

cat(
  "
  model {

    ####################
    #Priors
    ####################

    #detection parameters
    alpha[1] ~ dt(0, 1/6.25, 1) #cauchy(0, 2.5) priors
    alpha[2] ~ dt(0, 1/6.25, 1)

    #occupancy covariates
    beta[1] ~ dt(0, 1/6.25, 1)
    beta[2] ~ dt(0, 1/6.25, 1)

    ####################
    #Likelihood
    ####################

    #likelihood for latent states

    for(s in 1:n.sites){ #n.sites = no. of field sampling locations
      for(t in 1:T){ #T = no. of years sampled
        z[s,t] ~ dbern(psi[s,t]) #z[s,t] = latent occupancy state at site s in year t

        #site-specific occupancy probability
        l.psi[s,t] <- beta[1] + beta[2]*vegHt[s]
        psi[s,t] <- exp(l.psi[s,t])/(1+exp(l.psi[s,t]))
      }
    }

    #likelihood for observations in vertical format (not all sites sampled every year: i = ith observation in year t)

    for(t in 1:T){
      for(i in 1:n[t]){ #n = vector of number of sites sampled by year

        #sampling-event specific detection probability
        l.p[i,t] <- alpha[1] + alpha[2]*wind[i,t]
        p[i,t] <- exp(l.p[i,t])/(1+exp(l.p[i,t]))
        eff.p[i,t] <- z[sites[i,t],t]*p[i,t] #sites = matrix of site numbers (s indices from above) for observation i in year t
        y[i,t] ~ dbern(eff.p[i,t])
      }
    }

#Calculating integrated likelihood and log-posterior predictive scores for testing data set

for(t in 1:T2){ # T = no. of years sampled in testing data set
for(s in 1:sites2[t]){ # sites2 = vector of no. of sites in testing data by year
l.psi2[s,t] <- beta[1] + beta[2]*vegHt2[s]
psi2[s,t] <- exp(l.psi2[s,t])/(1+exp(l.psi2[s,t]))
for(v in 1:total.visits[s,t]){

#total.visits = matrix with total number of visits for site s in year t in testing data
#calculate p for each visit as a function of covariate values and regression coefficients

l.pnew[s,v,t] <- alpha[1] + alpha[2]*wind2[s,v,t]
p.new <http://p.new>[s,v,t] <- exp(l.pnew[s,v,t])/(1+exp(l.pnew[s,v,t]))
prob1[s,v,t] <- pow(p.new <http://p.new>[s,v,t], y2[s,v,t])*pow((1-p.new <http://1-p.new>[s,v,t]),(1-y2[s,v,t]))
prob2[s,v,t] <- 1-p.new <http://1-p.new>[s,v,t]
}

#see Appendix S1 for integrated likelihood and log-score formulae
term1[s,t] <- indicator[s,t]*psi2[s,t]*prod(prob1[s,1:total.visits[s,t],t])
term2[s,t] <- (1-indicator[s,t])*((1-psi2[s,t]) + psi2[s,t]*prod(prob2[s,1:total.visits[s,t],t]))
y.prob[s,t] <- term1[s,t] + term2[s,t]
lprob.y[s,t] <- log(y.prob[s,t])
}
score.t[t] <- sum(lprob.y[1:sites2[t],t]) #see S1.2
}
l.score <- -2*sum(score.t)

  }
"
)

sink()

# Inits

inits <- function() {
  list(
    z = z.wide.train,
    alpha = c(-1,-3) + rnorm(2),
    beta = c(-2, 2) + rnorm(2)
  )
}

# Parameters monitored
params <- c("alpha", "beta", "l.score")

# MCMC settings
ni <- 20000; nt <- 10; nb <- 10000; nc <- 3

# Call JAGS from R and summarize posteriors
SCtest <-
  jagsUI::jags(
    jags_data,
    inits = inits,
    params,
    "SC_mod.txt",
    n.chains = nc,
    n.thin = nt,
    n.iter = ni,
    n.burnin = nb,
    parallel = TRUE
  )

Hello all,

I am building a multistate model with survival and two different types of recruitment for a long-lived animal species using JAGS. My data includes live encounters and dead recoveries. From one occasion to another, my model includes three different possibilities in terms of recruitment: "recruitment of type A", "recruitment of type B" and "not recruited".This implies having to constraint recruitment probabilities to sum to 1 altogether using a Dirichlet prior following Kéry and Schaub (2012), which successfully worked in my models. However, my next step is to add an age structure with 5 age classes to all types of recruitment, and I am struggling to find a correct way to model this: I've tried several coding alternatives and I keep getting error notes.

Here's the code for modelling recruitments as constant probabilities:

#States:
#1: Alive, not recruited
#2: Alive, recruited A
#3: Alive, recruited B
#4: Dead, not recruited
#5: Dead, recruited
#6: Long-dead

    model{
    #Priors and constraints
    for(i in 1:nind){
    for(t in f[i]:(n.occasions-1)){

    p[i,t] <- recap[ages[i,t]]
    r[i,t] <- mean.r
    }#t

    for(u in 1:5){
    surv[u] ~ dunif(0,1)
    recap[u] ~ dunif(0,1)

    #Gamma priors for recruitment and emigration (Dirichlet)
    for (i in 1:3){ #1: not recruiting, 2: recruitment A, 3: recruitment B
    a[i] ~ dgamma(1,1) #Hyperprior for recruitment
    psiR[i] <- a[i]/sum(a[])
    }
    #Define state-transition and observation matrices
    for(i in 1:nind){
    for(t in f[i]:(n.occasions-1)){
    #State transition matrix
    ps[1,i,t,1] <- phi[i,t]*psiR[1] #Not recruiting

    ps[5,i,t,6] <- 1
    ps[6,i,t,1] <- 0
    ps[6,i,t,2] <- 0
    ps[6,i,t,3] <- 0
    ps[6,i,t,4] <- 0
    ps[6,i,t,5] <- 0
    ps[6,i,t,6] <- 1
    #Observation probabilities
    po[1,i,t,1] <- p[i,t]
    po[1,i,t,2] <- 0
    po[1,i,t,3] <- 0
    po[1,i,t,4] <- 0
    po[1,i,t,5] <- 0
    po[1,i,t,6] <- 1-p[i,t]
    po[2,i,t,1] <- 0
    po[2,i,t,2] <- p[i,t]
    po[2,i,t,3] <- 0
    po[2,i,t,4] <- 0

    po[2,i,t,6] <- 1-p[i,t]
    po[3,i,t,1] <- 0

    po[3,i,t,4] <- 0

    po[4,i,t,1] <- 0
    po[4,i,t,2] <- 0

    po[4,i,t,4] <- 1
    po[4,i,t,5] <- 0
    po[4,i,t,6] <- 0
    po[5,i,t,1] <- 0
    po[5,i,t,2] <- 0
    po[5,i,t,3] <- 0
    po[5,i,t,4] <- 0
    po[5,i,t,5] <- 1
    po[5,i,t,6] <- 0

    po[6,i,t,2] <- 0
    po[6,i,t,3] <- 0
    po[6,i,t,4] <- 0
    po[6,i,t,5] <- 0
    po[6,i,t,6] <- 1
      }#t

} #t
} #i
}
    ",fill=TRUE)

Any ideas or suggestions would be very appreciated. Please let me know if you need any further details.

Happy new year all! Thanks,

Jaume
